question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the core Claw lifecycle, including consented package-authored workspace instructions and their persistent ownership and recovery model?
rationale: The implementation is now technically coherent, but automation cannot authorize a new package-to-agent instruction trust boundary or commit core to the associated multi-PR lifecycle contract.

options.title: Pause for RFC approval
options.body: Keep the protected stack open and do not land mutation until maintainers approve the product model, trust boundary, and minimum recovery lifecycle.

options.title: Sponsor the lifecycle
options.body: Approve the direction and land the stack in dependency order with explicit consent, upgrade, and partial-state recovery guarantees.

options.title: Decline core adoption
options.body: Close the associated implementation stack if package-managed agent lifecycles are outside OpenClaw's intended core boundary.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC approval
recommendation.body: Keep the protected stack open and do not land mutation until maintainers approve the product model, trust boundary, and minimum recovery lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC discussion identifies this reviewer as the clearest available owner of the unresolved product-model question.
